id.description: the provider's id for it, echoed in the result

source.description: optional: the request or other entity this call came from

result.description: What a tool returned, and how long the call took.

ms.description: how long the tool took, in milliseconds

call.description: the call it is the result of

output.description: What produced the text beside it: the request, for a model’s own output; the call whose failure is being reported; or the stream it was read from (@yaks/process). Only output carries it — text a person or a system wrote has none.

source.description: the entry or run that produced it

id.description: the provider's id for this piece of output, as `call.id` is its id for the call — what a later revision of the same item is matched on

phase.description: which part of the answer it is — a model that narrates before it answers marks the narration apart from the answer

error.description: A failure the code expected and recorded. Normal operation.

exception.description: A failure the code did not expect, whoever caused it: a defect report, not a stop. On its own, its message is on the `content` component beside it; these columns are filled in by whichever process caught the error, and by nobody else.

stack.description: the stack trace, as the runtime reported it

request.description: what was being served when it threw

execution.description: How a recorded call is going, and which process is running it. `running` is that process’s claim on the call — a second server, or a re-entry, leaves it alone; a row still `running` when a process starts is a run that was interrupted, and the boot sweep runs it again. `by` names WHO is running it: a runner takes a call nobody holds, or one it holds itself, and never one held by somebody else — which is how a transcript imported from elsewhere arrives already executed.

by.description: the server or process running it

tool.description: A registered tool that callers can invoke.

call_ready.description: a call nobody has run and nobody scheduled: run the tool it names and attach the result

call_woken.description: a scheduled call whose wake has fired and that nobody has run yet: run it now. Never matches in a graph that does not load the wake components, where `call_ready` alone applies and every call is due when it is written
